title.en: Language work for A Concrete Example: words in context, instruments and notices

text.en: A poem about a sundial and a flower that was stepped on gives us a handful of useful language ideas: choosing the exact word, knowing what different instruments are called, saying sorry properly, and writing a notice that gets the message across.

keepEnglishTerms: new words by changing the first letter

text.en:
When you replace a word in a sentence, pick the one that fits the meaning there. 'A strange device' means an unusual one, 'delicate' flowers are fragile, and to say 'I cried' in a loud surprise is to exclaim.
In the poem the sundial is called a device, a thing made for a purpose. English has several related words for things we use, and they are not all the same.
An implement is something that works by being moved by hand, such as a spade or a knife. A tool is used by hand to make or repair something, such as a hammer.
Equipment is a set of necessary items for a particular purpose, such as a cricket bat, helmet and batting gloves. An appliance is an electrical device used to do work in the house, such as a mixer grinder.
A gadget is a small mechanical or electronic device, such as a mobile phone or a laptop.
You can make new words by changing only the first letter. Nice becomes dice, rice or mice, and soil becomes boil, toil, coil or foil. Clues in the meaning tell you which new word you need.
When we make a mistake we should apologise. With friends and family we use informal language, say sorry honestly, and the other person responds kindly. With elders or officials we use more formal language.
A notice informs many people about an event. State the purpose, date, time and venue, and whom to contact. Use formal language in the third person, write it in a box, and give the name of the organisation, the title NOTICE, the date, and the writer's name, class and signature.

problem.en: Match each item with the right word: a hammer, a mixer grinder, a cricket bat with a helmet, a spade, a mobile phone. Choose from implement, tool, equipment, appliance, gadget.

text.en: A hammer is used by hand to make or repair something: it is a tool.

why.en: Check what it is used for.

text.en: A mixer grinder is electrical and used for work in the house: it is an appliance.

why.en: Electrical and used at home means appliance.

text.en: A cricket bat with a helmet is a set of items for a purpose: it is equipment.

why.en: A set of necessary items means equipment.

text.en: A spade works by being moved by hand: it is an implement.

why.en: Moved by hand points to implement.

text.en: A mobile phone is a small electronic device: it is a gadget.

prompt.en: Draft the opening lines of a notice for the school Nature Club about a Herb Garden inauguration. Which details must it include and in which person is it written?

requiredIdeas.en: Purpose, date, time, venue and contact person
Formal language in the third person
Written in a box with the organisation name, title, date, writer's name, class and signature

commonMisconceptions.en: Writing a notice as a personal letter in the first person
Leaving out the date or venue

points.en: Choose the word that fits the meaning in the sentence.
Implement, tool, equipment, appliance and gadget mean different things.
New words come from changing the first letter: nice-rice, soil-boil.
A notice states purpose, date, time, venue and contact, in formal third person, inside a box.
